data.name: Abednego
data.gender_notes: Abednego is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Hebrew, the name Abednego means 'servant of God'. This name is prominent in the Old Testament, where Abednego is one of three Hebrew men who refuse to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's golden image. Their unwavering faith and loyalty to God are celebrated in the story. The name Abednego carries the meaning “Servant of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Abednego usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unwavering faith and commitment to God.
data.etymology: Abednego belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abednego total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: עבדנגו
in_hebrew.meaning: עבד ל אלוהים גדול נגו שפחה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עבדנגו הוא שם שמקורו בשפה הארמית ומשמעותו 'עבד נגו' או 'שפחה של נגו', כאשר 'נגו' הוא שם של אלוהים או כוכב לכת. השם עבדנגו מוזכר בספר דניאל בתנך, כחלק מהשמות של שלושת החברים של נבוכדנצר, מלך בבל.

in_greek.name: Αβδενηγώ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αβδενηγώ προέρχεται από την αρamaϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'υπηρέτης του Νεβουκαδνεσάρ' ή 'υπηρέτης του θεού Νεγώ'. Στη Βίβλο, το Αβδενηγώ αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους τρεις φίλους του προφήτη Δανιήλ, που ήταν επίσης υπηρέτες του βασιλιά Νεβουκαδνεσάρ Β' της Βαβυλώνας.

in_latin.name: Abdenego
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Abdenego derivatur ex lingua aramaea et significat 'servus Dei' vel 'servus Nego', Nego autem nomen est dei vel planetae. In libro Danielis, Abdenego est unus ex tribus amicis prophetae Danielis, qui fuerunt etiam servi regis Nabuchodonosoris, Babylonis regis.

in_english.name: Abednego
in_english.meaning: servant of Nego or servant of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Abednego originates from the Aramaic language, meaning 'servant of Nego' or 'servant of God'. It is biblically referenced in the book of Daniel as one of the three friends of the prophet Daniel, who were also servants of King Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon. The name holds significant spiritual meaning in Christian tradition, symbolizing servanthood and devotion to God.

data.cultural_impact: Abednego is a name that carries a rich history and cultural significance. It is a reminder of the strength and unwavering faith of the Hebrew people in the face of oppression and foreign rule. The story of Abednego, Shadrach, and Meshach is a powerful tale of defiance and courage, demonstrating the enduring resilience of the Hebrew people and their unwavering commitment to their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Abednego carries a deep spiritual significance as it serves as a reminder of the importance of remaining faithful to God and trusting in His plan for our lives. This name inspires us to stay steadfast in our faith, even in the midst of trials and challenges, and to trust in God's endless love and mercy. The story of Abednego, Shadrach, and Meshach teaches us that no matter what trials we may face, God is always with us and will carry us through.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Abednego means "servant of Nadab," in Hebrew. This name embodies the faith and unwavering devotion of the biblical figure, who with his companions Shadrach and Meshach, refused to bow down to King Nebuchadnezzar's idol, demonstrating their commitment to their God above all else.

biblical_reference.note: One of the three friends of Daniel, also known as Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Biblical account of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the Old Testament Book of Daniel. The name Abednego carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Three Israelites who refused to bow down to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.

trends: As a given name for boys
modern_usage.modern_context: Abednego is a name of Hebrew origin, derived from the Hebrew word 'abed' meaning servant. It is most commonly used as a given name for boys, and is also found as a surname. In modern times, the name has been used on various social media platforms and email addresses.

name_in_real_life.story: James Abednego from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Abednego - "Servant of God". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
